Title: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy - Habits That Slow Nerve Damage

Description:
The CDC estimates about 7 million American adults live with diabetic peripheral neuropathy. High blood sugar damages both the nerves and the tiny blood vessels that feed them, so numbness and tingling usually start in the toes and fingers first.

Poorly controlled blood sugar over time, plus high blood pressure and heart disease, both raise the risk of nerve damage. And once you can't feel your feet, small cuts and blisters go unnoticed - up to a third of people with diabetes develop a foot ulcer, and amputation risk jumps from about 11% to 29% if blood flow to the foot is also poor. Keep blood sugar, blood pressure, and cholesterol all in range, and check your feet every day.
